content: Disodium hydrogen phosphate (Na2HPO4) is a sodium salt derived from phosphoric acid. It appears as a white powder that is highly hygroscopic, meaning it readily absorbs moisture from the air, and it is also highly soluble in water. Due to these properties, it is commonly utilized in commercial applications as an anti-caking agent in powdered products to prevent clumping. This compound is also referred to by other names, including disodium hydrogen orthophosphate, sodium hydrogen phosphate, or sodium phosphate dibasic. It is available for commercial use in both hydrated and anhydrous forms. Disodium phosphate has additional applications in various industries. For instance, it is used in the preparation of cream of wheat to reduce the cooking time, enhancing convenience for consumers. Furthermore, it is employed in combination with trisodium phosphate in numerous steam boiler systems. In this context, it serves an important role by providing a source of free phosphates, which help to inhibit the formation of calcium scale deposits, thereby improving the efficiency and longevity of the boiler system.
